title: Stabilize runtime kernel routing after mixed-precision attention regression
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: On 2026-03-09 we observed a sustained uptick in p95/p99 token latency and token cost for several hosted models after a scheduler heuristic change. Root cause analysis shows the scheduler began routing a subset of requests to mixed-precision/quantized kernels that were incompatible with the current KV cache layout and attention tiling heuristics for long-context samples. This mismatch increased cache misses and triggered fallback behavior that amplified per-request latency and token compute. Impact: increased p99 latency by ~2.3x on affected paths, ~7% higher token cost for those routes, and customer-facing slowdowns for chat/streaming sessions during peak windows. Scope: ~8% of requests routed through the affected path across two high-traffic routes; predominantly long-context chat workloads using the 32k token profile. Objective: implement short-term safeguards to stop incorrect kernel routing, restore prior tail-latency SLOs, and deliver long-term preventative changes to kernel selector, scheduler policies, and canary testing to avoid regression recurrence.

root_cause: A heuristic change in the scheduler kernel-affinity scoring inadvertently favored mixed-precision/quantized kernels for sequences where the KV cache alignment and attention tiling required a different codepath. Mixed-precision kernels had subtle differences in KV cache layout expectations and attention prefetching behavior; when selected for long-context requests they caused increased cache misses and extra fallback processing in the runtime. There was insufficient canary coverage for long-context streaming workloads, and no runtime-level sanity check to validate kernel<->cache compatibility before routing production traffic.
mitigations: Immediate: Revert scheduler heuristic change rolled out on 2026-03-09 (completed during incident) to restore previous routing behavior
Short-term: Add a runtime validation gate that rejects kernel routing choices if kernel compatibility matrix does not match model config (safe-fallback to conservative CPU/GPU kernel)
Short-term: Add a scheduler-side conservative bias for mixed-precision kernels on long-context routes until compatibility testing is completed
Monitoring: Create dedicated Grafana panels for kernel-route distribution, KV cache miss rate by kernel, and per-kernel tail latency
Customer comms: Notify impacted customers via status page and a follow-up note with mitigation summary and planned timeline
